description: GitHub-based automated collection method for CRA Annex I assessment of open-source projects. Scripts require bash, curl, jq, and python3. Set all $PARAMETER environment variables before execution. Set GITHUB_TOKEN for authenticated requests (recommended: unauthenticated requests are rate-limited to 60/h).

OWNER.description: GitHub organisation or user owning the repository

ORG.description: GitHub organisation for organisation-level checks (may equal OWNER)

CONFIG_ENTRIES_PATH.description: Repository path to the product configuration entry point

AUTH_PATH.description: Repository path to the authentication module entry point

ONBOARDING_PATH.description: Repository path to the mandatory first-run setup component

RECORDER_PATH.description: Repository path to the persistent data storage component

CLOUD_INTEGRATIONS_PATH.description: Repository path to the directory containing external service integrations

API_PATH.description: Repository path to the network API component

HTTP_PATH.description: Repository path to the HTTP or TLS configuration module

ANALYTICS_PATH.description: Repository path to the analytics or telemetry configuration file

LOGBOOK_PATH.description: Repository path to the security event logging component

COMPONENTS_DIR.description: Repository path to the directory containing integration or plugin subdirectories

CI_SECURITY_WORKFLOW.description: Repository path to the CI security scanning workflow file

PYTHON_CONFIG.description: Repository path to the Python project metadata file

ATTACK_SURFACE_THRESHOLD.description: Maximum number of integration subdirectories for has-limited-attack-surfaces to be true

RECENCY_THRESHOLD_DAYS.description: Maximum age in days of the latest release for has-available-security-updates to be true

ASSESSMENT_DATE.description: ISO 8601 date of the assessment used for recency calculations

RELEASE_TAG.description: Git tag of the release being assessed

COMMIT_SHA.description: Full commit SHA of the assessed release; auto-resolved from RELEASE_TAG by collect.py if empty

operands.name: product/has-digital-element
operands.question: Does the product include digital elements (software or connected components)?
operands.heuristic: true if the repository's primary programming language field is not null, indicating the presence of executable software code
operands.script: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO" | jq 'if type == "object" and has("message") then empty else .language != null end'

operands.name: product/has-available-security-updates
operands.question: Are security updates currently available for the product?
operands.heuristic: true if the pinned release (RELEASE_TAG) was published within RECENCY_THRESHOLD_DAYS days of ASSESSMENT_DATE
operands.script:
RELEASE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/releases/tags/$RELEASE_TAG" | jq -r 'if has("message") then empty else .published_at[:10] end')
[ -z "$RELEASE" ] && exit 0
python3 -c "from datetime import date; print(str((date.fromisoformat('$ASSESSMENT_DATE') - date.fromisoformat('$RELEASE')).days <= $RECENCY_THRESHOLD_DAYS).lower())"

operands.name: product/cybersecurity-level
operands.question: What is the cybersecurity level of the product?
operands.artifact: Manual assessment — consult GET /repos/{OWNER}/{REPO}/security-advisories as supporting evidence
operands.heuristic: Level 1 (Low): no critical or high-severity unpatched advisories, product not listed in CRA Annex III. Level 3 (Moderate): unpatched advisories of moderate severity exist, or the product integrates with safety-sensitive physical devices. Level 5 (High): critical or high-severity unpatched advisories exist, or the product is listed in CRA Annex III or deployed in critical infrastructure. Compliance requires product/cybersecurity-level >= values/appropriate-level.

operands.name: product/is-free-of-known-exploitable-vulnerabilities
operands.question: Does the product have known exploitable vulnerabilities that are currently unpatched?
operands.heuristic: true if all published advisories (up to ASSESSMENT_DATE) have at least one vulnerability entry with a non-null patched_versions field, confirming no currently unpatched exploitable vulnerability exists
operands.script: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/security-advisories?per_page=100&state=published" | jq --arg d "$ASSESSMENT_DATE" 'if type != "array" then empty else ([.[] | select(.published_at[:10] <= $d)] | length > 0 and all(.[]; (.vulnerabilities | length) > 0 and all(.vulnerabilities[]; .patched_versions != null))) end'

operands.name: product/ensure-integrity
operands.question: Does the product ensure integrity of data and processing?
operands.artifact: GET /repos/{OWNER}/{REPO}/contents/.github/workflows?ref={COMMIT_SHA} — workflow file contents for cosign keyword
operands.heuristic: true if any CI workflow file in .github/workflows references cosign, evidencing that container images are cryptographically signed via Sigstore
operands.script:
WORKFLOWS=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/.github/workflows?ref=$COMMIT_SHA" | jq -r 'if type != "array" then empty else [.[] | select(.type == "file")] | .[].download_url end')
[ -z "$WORKFLOWS" ] && exit 0
FOUND=false
while IFS= read -r url; do
  if curl -s "$url" | grep -qi 'cosign'; then
    FOUND=true
    break
  fi
done <<< "$WORKFLOWS"
echo $FOUND

operands.name: product/is-updatable
operands.question: Can the product receive security updates after deployment?
operands.heuristic: true if the repository has at least one release published on or before ASSESSMENT_DATE, evidencing that a distribution mechanism exists through which users can apply updates. Manually verify that all supported deployment paths (package manager, container, OTA) provide a functional update mechanism and that users are notified of available updates.
operands.script: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/releases?per_page=100" | jq --arg d "$ASSESSMENT_DATE" 'if type != "array" then empty else ([.[] | select(.published_at[:10] <= $d)] | length > 0) end'

operands.name: product/document-product-vulnerabilities-and-components
operands.question: Are vulnerabilities and software components documented (e.g. SBOM)?
operands.heuristic: true if the GitHub dependency graph SBOM endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a valid SPDX 2.3 document. Note: this endpoint generates the SBOM from the default branch, not a pinned release tag; downstream manufacturers requiring a release-frozen SBOM must generate it independently.
operands.script:
STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/dependency-graph/sbom")
[ "$STATUS" = "200" ] && echo true; [ "$STATUS" = "404" ] && echo false

operands.name: product/product-vulnerabilities-are-remediated
operands.question: Are identified vulnerabilities remediated in a timely manner?
operands.heuristic: true if all published advisories (up to ASSESSMENT_DATE) have at least one vulnerability entry with a non-null patched_versions field, indicating all disclosed vulnerabilities have been remediated
operands.script: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/security-advisories?per_page=100&state=published" | jq --arg d "$ASSESSMENT_DATE" 'if type != "array" then empty else ([.[] | select(.published_at[:10] <= $d)] | all(.[]; (.vulnerabilities | length) > 0 and all(.vulnerabilities[]; .patched_versions != null))) end'

operands.name: product/publically-disclose-security-updates
operands.question: Are security updates and fixes publicly disclosed?
operands.heuristic: true if all published security advisories (up to ASSESSMENT_DATE) carry assigned CVE identifiers (100% CVE coverage), confirming public disclosure through the NVD
operands.script: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/security-advisories?per_page=100&state=published" | jq --arg d "$ASSESSMENT_DATE" 'if type != "array" then empty else ([.[] | select(.published_at[:10] <= $d)] | length > 0 and all(.[]; .cve_id != null)) end'

operands.name: product/has-enforced-vulnerability-disclosure
operands.question: Is there a formal vulnerability disclosure process in place?
operands.heuristic: true if a SECURITY.md file is accessible at either the organisation level (ORG/.github repository) or the repository level, confirming a documented coordinated disclosure process
operands.script:
ORG_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$ORG/.github/contents/SECURITY.md")
REPO_STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/SECURITY.md")
([ "$ORG_STATUS" = "200" ] || [ "$REPO_STATUS" = "200" ]) && echo true
([ "$ORG_STATUS" = "404" ] && [ "$REPO_STATUS" = "404" ]) && echo false

operands.name: product/has-shared-product-vulnerabilities
operands.question: Are known vulnerabilities shared with relevant stakeholders?
operands.heuristic: true if all published security advisories (up to ASSESSMENT_DATE) carry CVE identifiers, enabling automatic ingestion by vulnerability scanners and NVD cross-referencing by downstream manufacturers
operands.script: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/security-advisories?per_page=100&state=published" | jq --arg d "$ASSESSMENT_DATE" 'if type != "array" then empty else ([.[] | select(.published_at[:10] <= $d)] | length > 0 and all(.[]; .cve_id != null)) end'

operands.name: product/has-security-updates-securely-distributed
operands.question: Are security updates distributed through secure mechanisms?
operands.heuristic: true only if all supported deployment paths provide cryptographically signed update artefacts. false if any path (e.g. package manager) relies solely on transport-level integrity (HTTPS + checksums) without package-level signatures. Manually verify signing for container registry and OTA paths.
operands.script: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/releases/tags/$RELEASE_TAG" | jq 'if has("message") then empty else [.assets[].name | select(endswith(".sig") or endswith(".asc") or endswith(".sigstore"))] | length > 0 end'

operands.name: product/security-updates-are-free-and-quickly-disseminated
operands.question: Are security updates provided free of charge and distributed without delay?
operands.artifact: GET /repos/{OWNER}/{REPO} — license field; GET /repos/{OWNER}/{REPO}/releases — release timestamps
operands.heuristic: true if the repository licence is OSI-approved (implying free distribution) and the interval between the two most recent releases (up to ASSESSMENT_DATE) does not exceed RECENCY_THRESHOLD_DAYS
operands.script:
LICENSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO" | jq -r 'if has("message") then empty else .license.spdx_id // "NONE" end')
[ -z "$LICENSE" ] && exit 0
RELEASES=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/releases?per_page=100" | jq --arg d "$ASSESSMENT_DATE" 'if type != "array" then [] else [.[] | select(.published_at[:10] <= $d)] end')
LATEST=$(echo "$RELEASES" | jq -r '.[0].published_at[:10] // "1970-01-01"')
PREV=$(echo "$RELEASES" | jq -r '.[1].published_at[:10] // "1970-01-01"')
python3 -c "
from datetime import date
OSI = ['MIT','Apache-2.0','GPL-2.0','GPL-3.0','LGPL-2.1','LGPL-3.0','BSD-2-Clause','BSD-3-Clause','MPL-2.0','AGPL-3.0','ISC','CC0-1.0','Unlicense']
is_free = '$LICENSE' in OSI
cadence = (date.fromisoformat('$LATEST') - date.fromisoformat('$PREV')).days if '$PREV' != '1970-01-01' else 999
print(str(is_free and cadence <= $RECENCY_THRESHOLD_DAYS).lower())
"

operands.name: product/allow-configuration
operands.question: Can the product be configured or customised by the user?
operands.heuristic: true if the configuration entry point file or directory exists in the repository at the assessed commit
operands.script:
STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$CONFIG_ENTRIES_PATH?ref=$COMMIT_SHA")
[ "$STATUS" = "200" ] && echo true; [ "$STATUS" = "404" ] && echo false

operands.name: product/has-restricted-access
operands.question: Is access to the product restricted to authorised users only?
operands.heuristic: true if the authentication module entry point exists in the repository at the assessed commit, evidencing a deliberate access restriction implementation. Presence is a rebuttable presumption; effectiveness requires manual verification.
operands.script:
STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$AUTH_PATH?ref=$COMMIT_SHA")
[ "$STATUS" = "200" ] && echo true; [ "$STATUS" = "404" ] && echo false

operands.name: product/process-data
operands.question: Does the product process or store data?
operands.heuristic: true if the persistent data storage component directory exists in the repository at the assessed commit
operands.script:
STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$RECORDER_PATH?ref=$COMMIT_SHA")
[ "$STATUS" = "200" ] && echo true; [ "$STATUS" = "404" ] && echo false

operands.name: product/use-external-services
operands.question: Does the product rely on external services or third-party systems?
operands.heuristic: true if the external service integrations directory exists and contains files at the assessed commit, evidencing that the product connects to remote systems
operands.script: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$CLOUD_INTEGRATIONS_PATH?ref=$COMMIT_SHA" | jq 'if type == "object" and has("message") then empty else if type == "array" then length > 0 else false end end'

operands.name: product/has-digital-interface
operands.question: Does the product expose a digital interface (API, network interface)?
operands.heuristic: true if the network API component directory exists in the repository at the assessed commit
operands.script:
STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$API_PATH?ref=$COMMIT_SHA")
[ "$STATUS" = "200" ] && echo true; [ "$STATUS" = "404" ] && echo false

operands.name: product/has-secure-by-default-configuration
operands.question: Is the product configured securely by default?
operands.heuristic: true if (1) a mandatory onboarding component exists at the assessed commit, enforcing credential creation before first access, and (2) no hardcoded default password constant is found in the authentication module
operands.script:
ONBOARDING=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$ONBOARDING_PATH?ref=$COMMIT_SHA")
AUTH_CONTENT=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$AUTH_PATH?ref=$COMMIT_SHA" | jq -r '.content // ""' | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null)
if echo "$AUTH_CONTENT" | grep -qiE 'default_password|DEFAULT_PASSWORD'; then DEFAULT_PW=1; else DEFAULT_PW=0; fi
if [ "$ONBOARDING" = "200" ]; then
  [ "$DEFAULT_PW" -eq 0 ] && echo true || echo false
elif [ "$ONBOARDING" = "404" ]; then
  echo false
fi

operands.name: product/use-encrypted-data
operands.question: Is data encrypted at rest and in transit?
operands.heuristic: true if the HTTP or TLS configuration module exists at the assessed commit, evidencing that the product implements encrypted transport for data in transit
operands.script:
STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$HTTP_PATH?ref=$COMMIT_SHA")
[ "$STATUS" = "200" ] && echo true; [ "$STATUS" = "404" ] && echo false

operands.name: product/respect-minimisation-of-data
operands.question: Does the product collect and process only the minimum data required?
operands.heuristic: true if the analytics configuration uses an opt-in schema (all analytics preference fields are Optional rather than Required), evidencing that data collection is disabled by default
operands.script:
RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$ANALYTICS_PATH?ref=$COMMIT_SHA")
echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -e 'has("message")' >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0
CONTENT=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.content // ""' | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null)
echo "$CONTENT" | grep -qiE 'vol\.Optional|Optional.*bool|opt.?in' && echo true || echo false

operands.name: product/has-limited-attack-surfaces
operands.question: Is the attack surface minimised to what is strictly necessary?
operands.heuristic: true if the number of direct subdirectories in COMPONENTS_DIR does not exceed ATTACK_SURFACE_THRESHOLD. Each subdirectory represents an integration that may expose network connections or protocol listeners. Note: the git trees API response may be truncated for large repositories; check the truncated field.
operands.script:
DEPTH=$(awk -F'/' '{print NF}' <<< "$COMPONENTS_DIR")
COUNT=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/git/trees/$COMMIT_SHA?recursive=1" | jq --arg dir "${COMPONENTS_DIR}/" --argjson d $((DEPTH+1)) 'if type == "object" and has("message") then empty else [.tree[] | select(.type == "tree" and (.path | startswith($dir)) and (.path | split("/") | length == $d))] | length end')
[ -z "$COUNT" ] && exit 0
[ "$COUNT" -le "$ATTACK_SURFACE_THRESHOLD" ] && echo true || echo false

operands.name: product/is-using-exploitation-mitigation-mechanisms
operands.question: Does the product implement exploitation mitigation techniques (e.g. ASLR, DEP)?
operands.heuristic: true if the Python project configuration specifies a minimum Python version >= 3.12, ensuring that all supported runtimes include OS-level ASLR, DEP, and compiler hardening on all supported platforms
operands.script:
RESPONSE=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$PYTHON_CONFIG?ref=$COMMIT_SHA")
echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -e 'has("message")' >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0
CONTENT=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.content // ""' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null)
echo "$CONTENT" | grep -qE 'requires-python\s*=\s*">=3\.(1[2-9]|[2-9][0-9])' && echo true || echo false

operands.name: product/is-recording-security-information
operands.question: Does the product log and record security-relevant events?
operands.heuristic: true if the security event logging component directory exists in the repository at the assessed commit
operands.script:
STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$LOGBOOK_PATH?ref=$COMMIT_SHA")
[ "$STATUS" = "200" ] && echo true; [ "$STATUS" = "404" ] && echo false

operands.name: product/is-security-tested
operands.question: Is the product regularly tested for security vulnerabilities?
operands.heuristic: true if the CI security scanning workflow file exists at the assessed commit, evidencing automated security testing integrated into the development pipeline
operands.script:
STATUS=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/contents/$CI_SECURITY_WORKFLOW?ref=$COMMIT_SHA")
[ "$STATUS" = "200" ] && echo true; [ "$STATUS" = "404" ] && echo false

operands.name: product/has-control-access-mecanism
operands.question: Are access control mechanisms implemented (authentication, authorisation)?
operands.artifact: Manual review of authentication module and API token model
operands.heuristic: true only if (1) multi-factor authentication is enforced by default for all user accounts, and (2) API access tokens can be scoped to specific resources or integrations. A product where MFA is optional or where any token grants unrestricted access does not satisfy this operand.
operands.guidance: Review the authentication module for default MFA enforcement. Review the API token model for scope support. Check past CVEs for authentication bypass vulnerabilities. Verify whether a compromised token grants full system access.

operands.name: product/availability-of-essential-function
operands.question: Are essential functions protected against disruption or failure?
operands.artifact: Manual review of deployment architecture and process model
operands.heuristic: true if the product provides built-in high-availability or automatic recovery mechanisms for essential functions and documents a formal availability commitment. A single-process deployment with no redundancy and no SLA does not satisfy this operand.
operands.guidance: Assess whether the product runs as a single process or with built-in redundancy. Check for watchdog or supervisor mechanisms and whether they provide continuity guarantees or merely restart on failure. Verify whether a formal uptime commitment or SLA is documented.

operands.name: product/minimise-availability-issue-on-external-services
operands.question: Are risks from external service dependencies mitigated?
operands.artifact: Manual review of architecture documentation and offline behaviour
operands.heuristic: true if the product is designed to continue operating essential functions when external services are unavailable, through a local-first or offline-capable architecture
operands.guidance: Assess whether essential functions continue to execute when cloud or external services are offline. Check architecture documentation for explicit local-first design. Verify that the product degrades gracefully rather than failing completely on external service loss.

operands.name: values/appropriate-level
operands.question: What level of cybersecurity is appropriate for this product?
operands.artifact: CRA Annex III, CRA Annex IV, product deployment context
operands.heuristic: Regulatory determination based on CRA product classification and deployment context. Level 1 (Low): not listed in Annex III or IV, no integration with safety-sensitive devices. Level 3 (Moderate): not listed in Annex III, but typically deployed with safety-sensitive physical devices (door locks, alarm systems, cameras). Level 5 (High): listed in CRA Annex III or deployed in critical infrastructure contexts.
operands.guidance: Determine whether the product is listed in CRA Annex III (high-risk products) or Annex IV (third-party conformity assessment required). Consider the typical deployment context and whether the product integrates with safety-sensitive physical devices. Assign level 1 for purely informational consumer products, 3 for products with safety-sensitive integrations, and 5 for critical infrastructure or Annex III products.
